response.internal_assessment: Month eight coming up. I am at 70% on the EVT Level 2 and three months from the credential. The world outside is confirming every fear I had in a way that should feel vindicating but does not. A second robotaxi competitor in Millfield means this is not a pilot anymore — this is the market. Employment at 47% is not a statistic, it is the faces I see at the shop. Fewer cars coming in for service. Some of those people sold their cars; that is what the ownership number dropping to 21 out of 30 tells me. People who used to own cars and bring them to me are now in robotaxis. The mechanic demand index at 75 is still workable — I am still employed, still earning $5,800, still netting $193 a month. But the direction of travel is clear. Three months of certification left. I need to start thinking past the credential: who hires an EV-certified technician in a fleet context? RoboRide maintains a physical fleet. Someone wrench-turns those vehicles. That is the job I want positioned for when this training ends. Dale Cooper texted to thank me about Concord Lane — that is worth acknowledging and maintaining. The shop's foot traffic is softer. I can feel it in the daily schedule. Not a crisis yet, but the shop is leaning. My six-month-plus runway is still intact. I do not panic. I keep building.
response.inbox_interpretation: Two threads matter most. First: the second robotaxi competitor entering Millfield is a structural acceleration, not just competition for RoboRide. Two fleets means double the EV maintenance need in this locality — that is actually a green signal for my credential once I have it, not just a red signal for car ownership. Second: Dale Cooper's word-of-mouth item mentions texting me to thank me for the Concord Lane referral. That is a real social outcome and I should respond and maintain it — Dale owns a truck and trucks still need service, and a contractor with a working relationship with me is a customer and a referral source. The economy-wide collapse signals (spending index 29, employment 47%) are severe, but they are background — they reinforce the urgency of the credential without changing my immediate actions. Angela Wright is stressed; her word-of-mouth is about reaching out to people, not about me specifically. The EVT module outcome confirms 70% completion and another $193 saved. The SDV coursework this tick is direct preparation for servicing software-defined autonomous fleets — that is not coincidental with two robotaxi companies now in Millfield.

chosen_actions.description: Continue EVT Level 2 certification — month eight of ten. This month the coursework enters software-defined vehicle (SDV) remote diagnostics, over-the-air update protocols, and autonomous fleet maintenance procedures. This is not general EV training anymore — this is the specific technical language of the two fleets now operating in Millfield. Log at least 10 study hours across evening and weekend sessions. Do not negotiate with the fatigue. Three months remain. The credential is not hypothetical — it is weeks away.

resources.detail: EVT Level 2 progresses from 70% to approximately 80% completion. Module focus: SDV remote diagnostics, OTA update handling, autonomous fleet maintenance protocols — directly applicable to RoboRide and second competitor fleet maintenance.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The certification is three months from completion. This is not the moment to diversify effort — it is the moment to close. SDV content is exactly what the two robotaxi fleets in Millfield run on. The market just told me there will be more autonomous vehicles here, not fewer. The technician who can service them will have work. That technician is me in three months if I do not stop now.

chosen_actions.description: Respond to Dale Cooper's thank-you text about the Concord Lane referral with a brief, genuine reply. Acknowledge the thanks, mention that I am always glad to help when I can, and make natural reference to the shop — that if he ever needs anything for the truck, he knows where I am. No pitch, no desperation. Just keeping the thread alive.

resources.detail: A small investment of goodwill that maintains a relationship with a contractor who owns a truck and generates referrals. Costs nothing. Keeps a warm professional contact warm.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Dale reached out. In this economy, when someone reaches out, you respond. Contractors with trucks are among the last segment still actively maintaining vehicles because their work requires it. Dale at trust 0.44 is not a deep relationship, but it is one worth preserving with almost no cost. A text reply costs five minutes. Ignoring it costs more.

chosen_actions.description: Begin quietly researching which employers in the regional auto sector and fleet management sector hire EVT-certified technicians — specifically fleet maintenance roles connected to autonomous vehicle operators. Not applying yet. Not announcing it. Just mapping the landscape so that when the credential lands in three months, I am not starting from zero on where to take it. Look at RoboRide's public fleet maintenance documentation, regional dealership group job boards, and any fleet service contracts in adjacent cities.

resources.detail: A few hours of personal research time, evenings, not during shop hours. Intelligence-gathering only — no applications, no formal outreach yet.

chosen_actions.reasoning: A second robotaxi company in Millfield changes the math. There are now two fleets that need physical maintenance. I am three months from the credential that would qualify me for that work. If I wait until I have the credential in hand to begin understanding the hiring landscape, I have wasted three months. I do not jump ship from my current employment — I still earn and save — but I begin positioning so the transition, if it comes, is mine to make on my terms rather than the shop's.

response.inner_monologue: Two robotaxi companies now. Three months left on the cert. I am not going to pretend this is fine — the shop is quieter than it was a year ago and I know why. But I have been moving toward the thing that matters while the market moved under me, and I am not going to lose my footing this close to solid ground. Elena asked last week if I was sleeping enough. I told her mostly. That was honest enough.
